question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Although the set design by artist and director Andy Warhol surely shaped how the project was received, it was choreographer Merce Cunningham's application of his distinctive movement principles--including movement autonomy and chance procedure--to the collaborative dance piece RainForest that established ______ boldly transgressive aesthetic.
option a: his
option b: it's
option c: its
option d: they're
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The possessive 'its' correctly refers to the singular noun RainForest.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Eye color is an inherited characteristic. A parent might pass the blue-eye trait along to a child. ______ that child could go on to transmit the same trait to their own future biological children.
option a: Later,
option b: By contrast,
option c: For instance,
option d: Instead,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Later' signals the next stage in the sequence of generations.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Since 1972, the Women's Caucus for Art (WCA) has honored environmental artists such as Jo Hanson and installation artists such as Judy Chicago with Lifetime Achievement Awards for their contributions to the arts. ______ the WCA does not limit its push for gender equity in the arts to such recognition; the organization also gives women access to leadership and professional-development opportunities.
option a: For instance,
option b: However,
option c: As a result,
option d: Specifically,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'However' contrasts the awards with the WCA's additional efforts.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Plants called metal hyperaccumulators can pull heavy-metal contaminants out of soil. Sesbania drummondii, commonly known as rattlebush, for example, is able to take up large amounts of cadmium and lock it away safely in its roots and shoots. ______ its roots might not extend deep enough into the soil, potentially leaving small amounts of cadmium behind.
option a: Moreover, the plant is potentially useful in removing accumulated metals;
option b: That said, the plant may not always be able to remove all of the pollutant;
option c: On the contrary, a pollutant such as cadmium can be removed from the soil;
option d: For this reason, the plant has useful applications in soil quality restoration;
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'That said' concedes a limitation to the plant's cleanup ability.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? A character lets out a scream in the 1974 film The Scarlet Blade. ______ the actor shown on screen did not actually make that sound. It is the Wilhelm Scream, a sound effect featured in more than 200 films.
option a: Similarly,
option b: For example,
option c: However,
option d: As a result,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'However' contrasts the on-screen scream with its off-screen source.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to specify why Frances E. Allen won the A.M. Turing Award? While researching, a student compiled these notes: The A.M. Turing Award is a distinguished prize awarded by the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM). The ACM presents it for "major contributions of lasting importance to computing." Frances E. Allen received the award in 2006 for seminal contributions to optimizing compiler techniques.
option a: Generally, the prestigious A.M. Turing Award is given for "major contributions of lasting importance to computing."
option b: It was in 2006 that Frances E. Allen won the A.M. Turing Award.
option c: Frances E. Allen is a winner of the ACM's prestigious A.M. Turing Award.
option d: For seminal contributions to optimizing compiler techniques, Frances E. Allen won the A.M. Turing Award.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice D states the specific reason--her compiler-optimization work.

question: The student wants to compare how long the two sailors' voyages lasted. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Karen Leibovici is a French sailor. Benefic is a sailboat. Leibovici sailed Benefic around the world nonstop in 126 days. Lisa Clayton is a British sailor. Spirit of Birmingham is a sailboat. Clayton sailed Spirit of Birmingham around the world nonstop in 285 days.
option a: French sailor Karen Leibovici sailed Benefic around the world in 126 days.
option b: Clayton's 285-day journey around the world took longer than Leibovici's 126-day journey.
option c: Clayton's journey took place aboard Spirit of Birmingham, while Leibovici sailed on Benefic.
option d: Both Clayton and Leibovici embarked on sailing journeys around the world.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B directly compares the 285-day and 126-day durations.

question:
Which choice best describes data from the table that support the economists' claim?
Unit Cost in Dollars of Issuing US Coins by Denomination, 2020-2023
Year | One-cent | Five-cent | Ten-cent | Quarter-dollar
2020 | 0.0176 | 0.0742 | 0.0373 | 0.0862
2021 | 0.0210 | 0.0852 | 0.0439 | 0.0963
2022 | 0.0272 | 0.1041 | 0.0503 | 0.1111
2023 | 0.0307 | 0.1154 | 0.0530 | 0.1163
Because a Danish kroner coin's face value is higher than the unit cost of producing it, Denmark's government earns a profit--called seigniorage--by issuing the coin. Money from seigniorage can help fund parks and other government-supported amenities. Other nations, such as Sweden, have stopped issuing certain coins whose production cost surpassed their value, producing negative seigniorage. Some US economists argue that applying that same logic to the five-cent coin (worth 0.05 dollars) could raise the overall seigniorage the country earns from issuing all of its coins.
option a: In each year from 2020 to 2023, the unit cost of issuing a five-cent coin was greater than the unit cost of issuing a one-cent coin.
option b: The unit cost of issuing a five-cent coin rose more between 2022 and 2023 than the unit cost of issuing a ten-cent coin rose in that same period.
option c: From 2020 to 2023, the unit cost of issuing a five-cent coin ranged from more than 0.07 dollars to more than 0.11 dollars.
option d: In 2023, the unit cost of issuing a five-cent coin was 0.0530 dollars, greater than the face value of the coin.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice C accurately reads the rising five-cent unit cost from the table.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Whereas many poetry anthologies feature just one poem per poet, Heid E. Erdrich's New Poets of Native Nations offers ample selections from each. ______ Erdrich includes several poems by dg nanouk okpik and by Jennifer Elise Foerster. This lets readers explore a broad sampling of each poet's work.
option a: However,
option b: Next,
option c: In addition,
option d: For example,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'For example' introduces okpik and Foerster as instances of generous selection.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Smart watches and similar small gadgets usually house batteries that are difficult to ______ and swap for new ones. Environmental policy researcher Jessika Richter cautions that because these batteries cannot be taken out once they stop working, such devices have shorter life spans and quickly turn into waste.
option a: prevented
option b: imagined
option c: assembled
option d: removed
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Removed' fits batteries that cannot be taken out and replaced.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "produce" most nearly mean? The following text is from Oscar Wilde's 1893 play Lady Windermere's Fan.
MRS. ERLYNNE: I am going to live abroad again. The English climate doesn't suit me. My--heart is affected here, and that I don't like. I prefer living in the south. London is too full of fogs and--and serious people, Lord Windermere. Whether the fogs produce the serious people or whether the serious people produce the fogs, I don't know, but the whole thing rather gets on my nerves.
option a: Bring about
option b: Bind
option c: Make available
option d: Fancy
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: In context, 'produce' means to bring about or cause.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Drivers who firmly believe that the toll charged to cross the Teodoro Moscoso Bridge--which stretches across the San José Lagoon in Puerto Rico--is already too high are not likely to welcome a plan to raise it. Supporters of a toll increase would probably have more success if they instead aimed their arguments at a more ______ portion of the population.
option a: eminent
option b: persuadable
option c: knowledgeable
option d: frugal
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Persuadable' fits people more open to being convinced.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Aboard the sealed environment of the International Space Station, relative humidity is carefully controlled to keep microbes from growing out of control. Even so, Penicillium chrysogenum and other fungi--which have the potential to degrade spacecraft materials--may ______ whenever ordinary crew activities (such as showering) create pockets of humidity that climb above the maximum set for the station as a whole.
option a: abate
option b: recalibrate
option c: proliferate
option d: rehabilitate
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Proliferate' matches fungi multiplying in humid pockets.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Tikal, the celebrated Maya city in the lowlands of northern Guatemala, was probably ______ of the accomplishments made in the lesser-known polities of the Mirador Basin. As Morales-Aguilar et al. have demonstrated, the advances at those earlier Mirador sites (for instance, the ten astronomically aligned complexes at Nakbe) formed a historical precondition for the sophistication that the architects of later cities achieved.
option a: a replica
option b: a beneficiary
option c: an archetype
option d: an antithesis
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'A beneficiary' fits Tikal gaining from earlier Mirador achievements.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? Seigniorage is the gap between a coin's face value and the unit cost of making it. When seigniorage is positive, the issuing government earns revenue that can be used to fund education and other government-supported services. Some coins, however, cost more to make than they are worth. Although this has prompted certain countries, including Finland, to stop producing particular coins, another option is to alter the composition of some coins so that they are made with comparatively cheap metals.
option a: It details the rationale behind a particular economic decision made by Finland.
option b: It presents additional information to supplement a definition presented earlier in the text.
option c: It summarizes a method that the government of Finland uses to fund education.
option d: It indicates potential solutions to a problem discussed earlier in the text.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The final sentence offers approaches to the too-costly-coin problem.

question: Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? Vertical gene transfer passes genetic material from a parent to its offspring; horizontal gene transfer, by contrast, moves genetic material between organisms that are not in a parent-offspring relationship. Although horizontal gene transfer occurs often among prokaryotes--single-celled organisms such as the bacteria Carnobacterium viridans and Hafnia alvei--it has seldom been observed in eukaryotes, which are usually multicellular. Recent research, however, indicates that horizontal gene transfer happens more frequently in eukaryotes than was once believed.
option a: It implies that a common perception of horizontal gene transfer may be inaccurate.
option b: It compares the frequencies with which horizontal gene transfer has been detected in two categories of organisms.
option c: It indicates a distinction between horizontal gene transfer and vertical gene transfer.
option d: It argues that a particular direction of research concerning horizontal gene transfer is likely to be fruitless.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The last sentence suggests a common belief about the process may be wrong.

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? Jazz trumpeter Miles Davis, celebrated for albums such as Someday My Prince Will Come and Kind of Blue, worked with pianist Gil Evans on several occasions. Their 1958 take on George Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess departs sharply from the 1935 original. Davis and Evans had no interest in satisfying listeners who expected a faithful copy of the opera. They cut sections, such as the aria "I Got Plenty of Nuthin'," and at times only gestured briefly toward Gershwin's melodies. Yet their willingness to rework Gershwin's material produced one of the most lasting albums in Davis's catalog.
option a: Davis and Evans's adaptation of Porgy and Bess received a better critical reception than the work on which it was based.
option b: Davis's creative efforts became more experimental when he collaborated with Evans.
option c: Audiences for jazz music tend to prefer novelty over convention.
option d: Davis and Evans's confidence in revising Gershwin's opera led to the creation of one of Davis's most notable recordings.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The main point is that reworking the opera yielded a landmark Davis album.

question: Which quotation from "May-Day" most effectively illustrates the claim? "May-Day" is an 1867 poem by Ralph Waldo Emerson. In the poem, the speaker describes the sounds of nature: ______
option a: "The million-handed sculptor moulds / Quaintest bud and blossom folds, / The million-handed painter pours / Opal hues and purple dye."
option b: "Firm-braced I sought my ancient woods, / Struggling through the drifted roads; / The whited desert knew me not, / Snow-ridges masked each darling spot."
option c: "The sparrow meek, prophetic-eyed, / Her nest beside the snow-drift weaves, / Secure the [tree] yet will hide / Her callow brood in mantling leaves."
option d: "What was that I heard? / Harp of the wind, or song of bird, / Or vagrant booming of the air, / Voice of a meteor lost in day?"
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only D describes sounds--wind, birdsong, and booming air.

question:
Which choice best describes data from the table that support Pützelsberger and colleagues' conclusion?
Numbers of the 23 Non-native Tree Species Reported and the Insect and Fungus Threats to Them
Country | Trees | Fungi | Insects
Bulgaria | 9 | 14 | 16
Great Britain | 18 | 290 | 120
Slovakia | 15 | 28 | 53
Elisabeth Pützelsberger and colleagues collected data on 23 non-native tree species cultivated in Europe. Drawing on reports from Slovakia, Great Britain, and Bulgaria, they recorded how many of these species each country grows as well as the numbers of insect and fungus species that damage those trees. They concluded that only one of the three countries reported a greater number of damaging fungus species than damaging insect species.
option a: Great Britain reported 290 damaging fungus species and 120 damaging insect species, while both Slovakia and Bulgaria reported a greater number of damaging insect species than fungus species.
option b: Bulgaria reported 16 damaging insect species but only 14 damaging fungus species.
option c: Slovakia and Bulgaria both reported fewer damaging fungus species than damaging insect species, whereas Great Britain reported 120 fungus species and only 18 insect species.
option d: Great Britain reported 290 damaging fungus species, which is more than either Slovakia or Bulgaria reported.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A shows only Great Britain had more fungus than insect threats.

question: Which statement, if true, would most directly undermine the claim in the underlined sentence? Hawaiian Pidgin, a creole language, is mainly a blend of English and ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi (the language of the Native Hawaiian people), with added input from Okinawan, Spanish, and other East Asian and Romance languages. A hallmark of Hawaiian Pidgin grammar is the stative construction, in which a verb modifies the subject and serves a descriptive role much as an adjective does, as in "nice da stew" (nice the stew). Here "nice" acts as a verb whose subject is "da stew," so the phrase means "the stew is nice." Such constructions point to the influence of Okinawan and other East Asian languages, which likewise abound in stative structures in which verbs take on a descriptive function.
option a: Verbs capable of modifying subjects by themselves are absent from most English dialects, which instead use copular verbs--forms of "to be" (the sky is cloudy) or other verbs that help express a state of existence (the sky looks cloudy)--to link subjects to the adjectives that modify them.
option b: In Hawaiian Pidgin, a stative structure in which the verb precedes its subject is used for emphasis, while a structure in which the verb follows the subject (da stew nice) appears in unemphatic statements, and this sequence of verb and subject corresponds to that of stative structures in Okinawan and other East Asian languages.
option c: Stative structures in ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi often include an article equivalent to "the" in English, and their syntax corresponds to that of Hawaiian Pidgin stative structures, while Okinawan and other East Asian languages lack articles altogether.
option d: African American Vernacular English (AAVE) is one of the few US-based dialects of English with stative structures in which verbs modify subjects by themselves, but the syntax of those structures differs from that of Hawaiian Pidgin stative structures.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice C ties the construction to ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi, undercutting the East Asian-influence claim.
